chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Ṣafwān, from Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who begins the obligatory salat (prayer), then remembers that he did not pronounce the iqāmah. He said: “If he remembers that he did not pronounce the iqāmah before he recites, then let him send greetings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, then pronounce the iqāmah and perform salat (prayer). But if he remembers after he has recited part of the surah, then let him complete his salat (prayer).”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: All of these reports are to be understood as indicating recommendation, because when he has begun the salat (prayer), the basic principle is that it is permissible for him to continue in it, and he is not required to break off. What clarifies what we have mentioned is what he narrated:

key_terms.الِانْصِرَافُ: breaking off or withdrawing from the prayer
key_terms.بَعْضَ السُّورَةِ: a portion of the surah recited in prayer
key_terms.فَلْيُسَلِّمْ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ: let him send greetings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they remember during obligatory salat (prayer) that they did not say the iqāmah?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of one who begins an obligatory salat (prayer) and then remembers that he omitted the iqāmah. If he remembers before recitation, he may stop, send greetings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, pronounce the iqāmah, and begin again; but if he remembers after reciting part of the surah, he should complete the prayer. The compiler then explains that such reports are interpreted as recommending this practice rather than making it obligatory.
